class.name: UZUUIJuice
class.brief_description: UI motion: named movement curves and one-call animations for panels, dialogs, hover and numbers.
class.description: [UZUUIJuice] is the UI counterpart of [UZUJuice]: the movements that make a UI feel like a game, behind static calls. A runtime node is created in the scene tree on first use and advances the animations; every animation is a pure state value (elapsed time through a named curve), so it behaves the same in self-verifying play and its start and finish are written to an event log ([method get_event_log]). The motion vocabulary (from gameanimation.info, "UI no komakai ugoki") is a set of named curves, see [method get_preset_names]: [code]anticipation[/code] (a small move opposite to the main one first), [code]overshoot[/code] (past the goal, then back, with strength levels), [code]ease_in[/code] (a mechanical, braking stop), [code]bounce[/code], and [code]step[/code] (held frames, for pixel art). Which curve a world uses is decided by [method UZUUI.get_world_motion]; [method apply_world_motion] reads it, so a world's look and motion stay together. [codeblock] var dialog = UZUUI.make_dialog("Elder", "Bring three shards.", ["Accept"]) add_child(dialog) UZUUIJuice.open_panel(dialog) # overshoot by default UZUUIJuice.count_up(score_label, 0, 1200) UZUUIJuice.close_panel(dialog) # anticipation by default: a breath in, then out [/codeblock] Animations capture the control's scale, pivot and modulate and restore them exactly when they end or are cancelled. [b]Note:[/b] This class is specific to U.ZU Engine.

method.name: apply_animations
method.description: Advances every running animation by [param dt] seconds. Called by the runtime node each frame; tests and tools can call it directly with fixed steps.

method.name: apply_world_motion
method.description: Opens (or closes, with [param open] false) [param control] with the motion of a [UZUUI] world: the duration, overshoot and steps of [method UZUUI.get_world_motion] become the curve (a stepped world moves frame by frame, a world with a big overshoot snaps). Returns [code]false[/code] for an unknown world.

method.name: cancel
method.description: Stops the control's animation, restoring exactly what was captured when it started.

method.name: cancel_all
method.description: Stops every running animation, restoring each control.

method.name: clear_event_log
method.description: Empties the event log (see [method get_event_log]).

method.name: close_panel
method.description: Closes [param control]: shrinks it through the curve, then hides it, restoring its scale and pivot exactly. With the default [code]anticipation[/code] curve it first swells a little -- the classic dialog close.

method.name: count_up
method.description: Counts a [Label]'s text (or a [Range]'s value) from [param from] to [param to] through the curve. The final value is exact.

method.name: get_active_animation_count
method.description: Returns how many animations are running.

method.name: get_animation_state
method.description: Returns the running animation of [param control] as data, for probes and tests: [code]animating[/code], [code]motion[/code] (the B-1317 preset name; legacy animations report their event name), [code]curve[/code], [code]elapsed[/code], [code]duration[/code], [code]progress[/code] (the possibly step-quantized time, 0 to 1) and [code]value[/code] (the curve at that time). The driven state itself (scale, modulate) is read from the control. Just [code]{"animating": false}[/code] when idle.

method.name: get_event_log
method.description: Returns the event log: one dictionary per animation start and finish, with [code]event[/code] ([code]open[/code], [code]close[/code], [code]hover[/code], [code]count_up[/code], [code]transition[/code], and the B-1317 motions [code]appear[/code], [code]disappear[/code], [code]press[/code], [code]value_change[/code]), [code]phase[/code] ([code]start[/code] or [code]end[/code]), [code]preset[/code] and [code]target[/code] (the control's name). Self-verifying play (and tests) read this to confirm UI events fired. Capped at the newest 256 entries.

method.name: get_motion_names
method.description: Returns the motion presets of [method play_motion] (B-1317): [code]appear[/code], [code]disappear[/code], [code]hover[/code], [code]press[/code], [code]value_change[/code]. These name what a control does; [method get_preset_names] names the curves it moves through.

method.name: get_preset
method.description: Returns one curve as data: [code]name[/code], the default [code]duration[/code] and [code]strength[/code]. [code]overshoot[/code] also carries [code]overshoot_by_level[/code], the back constants of strength levels 1 to 3; [code]step[/code] carries [code]steps[/code]. An empty dictionary for an unknown name.

method.name: get_preset_names
method.description: Returns the named motion curves: [code]anticipation[/code], [code]overshoot[/code], [code]ease_in[/code], [code]bounce[/code], [code]step[/code].

method.name: hover_pulse
method.description: A one-shot swell for hover and presses: the control grows by 10% times [param strength] and comes back, ending at exactly the captured scale. Call it from a [code]mouse_entered[/code] or [code]pressed[/code] handler.

method.name: is_animating
method.description: Returns whether [param control] has a running animation (including as the incoming side of a [method transition]).

method.name: motion_value
method.description: The curve itself: the progress at time [param t] (0 to 1). The result may dip below 0 (anticipation) or rise above 1 (overshoot, bounce); both ends are exact (0 at 0, 1 at 1). [param strength] scales the anticipation dip and the overshoot. Pure math, with no scene tree or clock involved.

method.name: open_panel
method.description: Opens [param control]: shows it and grows it from nothing through the curve. The control's own scale and pivot are restored exactly when the animation ends.

method.name: overshoot_value
method.description: The overshoot curve at a strength level: 1 is soft, 2 is the classic back curve, 3 is sharp (the persona world's snap). Pure math.

method.name: play_motion
method.description: Plays one motion preset (see [method get_motion_names]) on [param control], in one call. [param options] may carry [code]world[/code] (a UZUUI world name: duration, curve, strength and steps come from the world's motion, so persona is fast with a big overshoot and pixel steps frame by frame; [code]value_change[/code] takes twice the world's duration), [code]curve[/code] (a curve name, overriding the world's), [code]duration[/code], [code]strength[/code], [code]steps[/code], and [code]to[/code] / [code]from[/code] (the [code]value_change[/code] endpoints; [code]from[/code] defaults to the current value, [code]to[/code] to a Range's max). Returns [code]false[/code] for an unknown motion, world or curve, and for [code]value_change[/code] on a control holding no value.

method.name: seek_animation
method.description: Sets the animation's clock to [param time] seconds and applies that exact state at once, so a probe or a test can sample any moment without waiting in real time. At or past the duration the animation finishes, with the exact end state. Returns [code]false[/code] when [param control] is not animating.

method.name: transition
method.description: The minimal screen transition: [param from_control] fades out and hides while [param to_control] fades in, both through the curve. Both controls' modulate and scale are restored exactly; the incoming control stays visible. Returns [code]false[/code] if either control is missing.
